findings.text: follow-on: the tightened count is not isolated by any control, and cannot be by throttling alone. The node's sweep (period/keep 2/1, 3/1, 3/2, 4/3, 5/4) shows every partial throttle fails BOTH arms at the thread.is_alive assertion (base line 110, head line 119), never at the count, because the lease's liveness already forces one write per half interval at the test's 1.5 s cadence, the very floor renewals >= 5 asserts. I confirmed this by reading runs.py:1257-1272 and recovery.py:8592-8607 and by the head arm re-run. A zero-write mutation (throttle every call) reddens the base arm too, at its advanced > fresh assertion, so it isolates neither arm's count. Decoupling liveness from the count (a scratch that refreshes lease_renewed_at outside the follower) is the only path to a clean isolation and is a larger change than this node's scope; the node reached the same conclusion and recorded it in 7e4066af6. Not a blocker: the count change is a correct semantic fix, it measures writes rather than non-None returns, even where its assertion is redundant with is_alive under this cadence.

runs.renew_producer_lease(...) is not None. reckon/ is unchanged across 3b883745b..7e4066af6

lease_renewed_at moves only at the producer's seat-take (runs.py:2035) and on a landed renewal

observed advance. I read the source and re-ran the head arm myself.

tested content and the head's test behaviour is unchanged.
